scope: Five new backend native PostgreSQL conditional-read and request-owned provider candidates beyond 429 immutable historical candidates.

passes.candidate: Read conditional sidebar metadata and changed trees in one fresh PostgreSQL row snapshot
passes.mechanism: An exact canonical UTC ETag masks ciphertext and row identity for 304. A changed request reads fresh version, decoded-cache mask and ciphertext together, releases its transaction, and constructs the response from that same snapshot. Subclasses keep their original public method dispatch.
passes.reason: Accepted for the deterministic removal of one SQL roundtrip from changed conditional reads of a freshly present valid cache row: two SELECTs become one. Matching 304 and no-header cached reads retain one SELECT. Misses and invalid rows retain the original fallback. Process latency measurements are local and noisy, so this is not a universal latency claim.

closestEarlierCandidate.candidate: Suppress warm sidebar ciphertext transfer only when a freshly read exact PostgreSQL tuple version matches the decoded tree

priorWorkAudit.whyNew: Earlier storage-r4-04 suppresses ciphertext only after a fresh exact tuple-version match. It still performs the separate conditional timestamp read. This candidate joins those conditional reads without replacing the prior tuple-identity policy.

passes.candidate: Share one native Drive SDK root between compatible request-owned Drive and Files services
passes.mechanism: A request-owned collaborator records exact user-object, Google subject, token revision, Google token generation, encrypted credential, expiry, handler and factory identities per SDK-owning thread. Files accepts that root only for the exact native Drive service and binding; mismatches retain the original per-service fallback.
passes.reason: Accepted for the deterministic removal of one native SDK discovery/root construction on the compatible serial request path: two roots become one. Exact final-source native controls and alternating within-process measurements qualify the retained collaborator. Warm and two-worker controls are retained as limits on the improvement.

closestEarlierCandidate.candidate: Build one Google files resource per synchronous metadata/probe worker instead of rebuilding it for each GET subrequest

priorWorkAudit.whyNew: Earlier provider-round4-02 reuses a files resource inside one synchronous metadata worker. This candidate shares the native root across two compatible services owned by the same request and thread; discovery JSON caching and request inventory tasks already existed and are not counted.

passes.candidate: Read a completed request inventory task directly while retaining shield for pending tasks
passes.mechanism: Replace shield on an already-completed request inventory task with public Task.result; pending work retains the original shield, task reset and list scan paths.
passes.reason: Rejected. The warm task call saves about 0.23 microseconds for one drive, but the complete installed HTTP route improves only 1.68%, within local variation; the added branch has no meaningful route benefit.

closestEarlierCandidate.candidate: Replace the shared singleflight result Future with the current leader caller Task.

priorWorkAudit.whyNew: Earlier round6-cache-07 changes shared singleflight result ownership to the caller task. This candidate changes only the already-completed request-local inventory await and retains pending-task shield and singleflight ownership.

passes.candidate: Validate recent-page response records through one public TypeAdapter(list[RecentFile])
passes.mechanism: Build the bounded public recent-page response through the public Pydantic list adapter, validate all accessible eligible inputs before the existing five-page slice, and preserve order and names.
passes.reason: Rejected. Complete native recent HTTP operations regress 2.48% for one item and 4.07% for six items; the response API and validation semantics remain correct.

closestEarlierCandidate.candidate: Validate Drive inventory metadata in bounded 64-record RootModel buffers

priorWorkAudit.whyNew: Earlier round6-bulk-02 validates Drive inventories in bounded 64-record RootModel buffers. This candidate targets the separate public RecentFile response records and bounded response route.

passes.candidate: Bind the public metadata model validator once per native multipart batch
passes.mechanism: Store model.model_validate once before the existing multipart callback loop; preserve exact public validation, retry, malformed-input and exception propagation paths.
passes.reason: Rejected. Complete native multipart metadata operations show mixed changes from -1.78% to +1.14%, including essentially no gain at 100 items; descriptor binding is not material beside native SDK and parsing work.

closestEarlierCandidate.candidate: Reuse an immutable absent-capabilities model for validated Google file inventories

priorWorkAudit.whyNew: Earlier provider-round4-04 reuses an immutable absent-capabilities model. This candidate changes public validator descriptor binding in the native multipart callback, with no validation bypass or schema default change.

sampleDesign.aggregation: Metrics use the median of all documented per-operation samples. Every process median, range, population standard deviation and raw sample is retained; no outlier or regression is deleted.

countZeroRefinements.action: Narrow the new test match parameter from str to its five-value Literal after the unchanged BasedPyright gate reported one non-exhaustive match. Application source bytes and test runtime behavior are unchanged; no suppression or configuration change was added.
Extract native SDK sharing into a request-owned collaborator to satisfy the unchanged public-method cap and private-member rules; preserve all earlier failed Ruff receipts.

Qualify exact Google token generation alongside existing subject, revision, credential, expiry, user, factory, handler and thread binding. Add native mismatch and refresh controls without adding a candidate.
Preserve the initial 187-passed/4-provider-skipped receipt and rerun the unchanged focused set with both task-owned URLs after the user/parent interruption.

Repeat exact final-source alternating native comparisons; preserve all earlier negative and noisy raw measurements. The resumed agent only narrowed the new test parameter annotation after the unchanged BasedPyright gate rejected str; application sources remained unchanged.

reproduce: Use the immutable baseline, prototype and final-resume source snapshots and recorded native runtime versions. Verify every SHA256 before reproduction; the baseline commit is d716fee43e906abf05aa40490f0d883c9e9164a3.

Run all measurements through sarj-wiki-perf-round10-benchmark-guard.py. The phase receipts contain exact command, cwd, synthetic local environment, log and output hashes. Use fresh paths; preserve existing evidence.

For native SDK pairs use backend-provider-paired-generation.py --pass-id 2 --variant final --samples 15 --iterations 8 --first-order baseline or candidate with fresh output names. Source snapshots bind both full baseline modules and the exact final modules; no methods are replaced.

For native PostgreSQL pairs use backend-sidebar-worker-v2.py --pass-id 1 --variant baseline or final --samples 9 --iterations 6 in alternating process order. It creates and drops only a fresh round10_backend_01_<variant>_<uuid> schema in the owned loopback reads database.

Rejected candidates 03-05 use their preserved complete prototype modules and provider-worker-v2.py with the recorded native process-pair commands. Their final runtime modules remain byte-equal to baseline for the rejected behavior.
limitations: These are synthetic installed native SDK, multipart, local PostgreSQL18.6 and ASGI operations. They do not measure production provider latency, live browser navigation, or production p95.

Candidate 01 removes one changed-conditional query for a present valid cache row. Matching 304 and no-header controls remain one-query paths; missing or invalid rows retain fallback behavior. Local elapsed times can vary and their raw regressions are retained.

Candidate 02 benefits the compatible serial cold request. Different users, credentials, generations, handlers, factories, subclasses or threads retain the original per-service construction. Warm and two-worker timings do not support a universal speedup.

An expired native credential refresh that changes the principal generation correctly declines the pre-refresh binding. Fresh provider metadata, authorization and malformed-input handling remain native on every request.
Preexisting schemas and relation OIDs are preserved. Measurement fixtures tear down only their own fresh schemas; focused tests clean only their newly seeded users and fixture rows.
Root owns unchanged full make check, central standards, git/hook/hosted CI work, user approval boundaries, original-workspace sync and authenticated live UX verification after scope sealing.
These five measured candidates do not prove that no future optimization is possible.
